rationale: The official O-220 member reports shiitake in one choking event and five patients with Parkinson disease, with no food-to-diagnosis link or preparation report. A case-linked follow-up is unverified. Modified food textures do not resolve the frozen comparison.

The viral olfaction review uses watermelon to explain flavor discrimination. The 2025 nutraceutical review has isolated-lycopene context, and clinical intake-frequency data do not report matched bradykinesia. Existing animal movement surrogates do not measure the frozen preparation and symptom.

The original cranberry guidance concerns recurrent urinary infections. PMID40442918 remains at abstract depth for the preparation and numerical motor outcomes. NCT07453537 is recruiting, reports no results and has no registered bradykinesia outcome.

FEBS member P039 uses cardamom extract in a rat bladder model. The individual menu component is not isolated in the Parkinson diet trial, which only reports a composite motor endpoint. No separate ground-cardamom and rigidity contrast was identified.

The WHO original distinguishes poison sumac from culinary Rhus coriaria. The full sumac-powder trial gives an inconclusive BDI-II comparison. The separate Golshani oral fruit essential-oil rat results and methods remain at abstract depth.

The 2018 ASENT member tests Nigella sativa, a different plant. Common cumin work studies aqueous extract or isolated cuminaldehyde, and Parkinson diet reports provide no isolated toasted ingredient or dyskinesia score.
